slides.say: Just moved to the Netherlands? You need this number before almost anything else.

slides.small: Your unique personal number for contact with the Dutch government.
slides.say: It's called a B S N, your citizen service number. A unique personal number for all your contact with the Dutch government.

slides.small: Moving here? Register within 5 days of arriving. You get your BSN when you register.
slides.say: You get it when you register with your municipality. If you come to live here, register within five days of arriving.

slides.small: Staying less than 4 months? 19 municipalities have an RNI desk for non-residents.
slides.say: Staying less than four months, or living abroad? Register at an R N I desk instead. Nineteen municipalities have one.

slides.small: Your employer, the tax office, care providers and health insurers use it.
slides.say: You'll need it for work, taxes, your doctor and your health insurance.

slides.big: DON'T SHARE IT WITH JUST ANYONE
slides.small: Only organisations allowed by law may use your BSN.
slides.say: And keep it safe. Only organisations that are allowed by law should ask for it.

slides.small: Follow so you don't miss it.
slides.say: Next up, DigiD, your Dutch government login. Follow so you don't miss it.
